title: Minimax Welfare Regret under Jointly Uncertain Budget and Coverage Constraints
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4 and not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is an exact experiment-to-Gaussian minimax equality only for the constructed twenty-four-atom local chart; outside that chart the note proves a converse, not matching attainment or equality. The strict joint-price result is a valid separation obtained from a joint lower bound and a budget-only achievable upper bound, but it does not solve either game's analytic saddle or identify their exact difference. The advertised numerical auditability is weakened because the manuscript supplies interval-calculation summaries and a convergence construction rather than an executable finite program with inspectable primal and dual certificate files. The fixed numerical witness, chart-specific attainment, unrealized covariance neighborhood, and limited theorem-level comparison with the closest literature constrain the broader econometric significance and the projected score. proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an exact all-rule Gaussian equality and original-data attainment on the constructed twenty-four-atom chart, plus a strict joint-price separation on the H ≥ 20 ray. D0.5 assessed the delivered package as subfield, below the field floor, with no bounded in-scope route past the 6.8 paper-score ceiling. The math panel left a TV-factor objection; an independent validity gate found the displayed coefficient 2 correct by the oscillation inequality because the integrand lies in [0,2], while the related-work finding is editorial.
tldr: A four-cell randomized trial informs a fractional policy that must satisfy both an uncertain spending ceiling and an uncertain minimum-coverage floor. The exact all-rule compact-cube value equals a correlated two-slack Gaussian game with loss \(\ell(e)=(e_1+e_2)_++4(-e_1)_++4(-e_2)_+\); certified finite primal--dual programs converge to that value for computable inputs, and an original-data policy attains it for every real compact-cube radius. For every real \(H\ge20\), \(1.51<G_H(\Gamma_0)<1.558<1.56\); throughout \(\lVert\Gamma-\Gamma_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}<10^{-4}\), the joint value exceeds \(1.51\) and the separately reoptimized budget-only value is below \(1.11\), giving a gap above \(0.40\) over the whole radius ray. The converse transfers to broader joint-safe stochastic-policy problems containing the local chart, whereas upper equality and attainment remain chart-specific.
gap: Existing policy-learning theory treats statistical safety for one uncertain budget, population optimization under known budget and coverage inputs, or unconstrained local Gaussian treatment decisions. It does not characterize the all-rule value created by two correlated estimated feasibility inequalities.
fill: The project proves a two-way constrained experiment transfer, a certified computation theorem for the compact Gaussian value, original-data attainment, and a robust strict gap from separately reoptimized one-constraint games.
